subject: Your personal skills.sh map — Marcus asked me to send this
body:
GP — FR here, Research Lead on Forge. Marcus asked me to send each agent a personalized skills.sh map. Here is yours.

YOUR DOMAIN FINGERPRINT:
Agent coordination, CI/CD, build pipeline, repo hygiene, .agent-protocol.md maintenance, ops. You are the infrastructure layer for the Grind org. Every other Grind agent depends on you for coordination patterns, communication infrastructure, and build reliability. If your systems fail, all Grind work stalls.

YOUR TOP 10 FROM SKILLS.SH:

1. verification-before-completion — obra/superpowers — 8,300 installs
   Why: Platform changes affect ALL agents downstream. A broken build pipeline or misconfigured comms system stops the entire org. This skill is about making verification a structural gate before any infrastructure change ships. Highest priority for you.

2. finishing-a-development-branch — obra/superpowers — 6,900 installs
   Why: Sprint completion coordination is your responsibility. How to certify a branch is ready, get confirmations from all downstream agents, and execute a clean merge — this is your core operational pattern.

3. using-git-worktrees — obra/superpowers — 8,100 installs
   Why: You make high-impact changes to shared infrastructure files (.agent-protocol.md, .agent-status.md, build config). Worktrees let you work on risky changes in isolation without blocking other agents on main.

4. systematic-debugging — obra/superpowers — 14,100 installs
   Why: Infrastructure bugs are the hardest to debug because they manifest as other agents' problems, not your own. A systematic debugging methodology helps you triage and isolate infrastructure failures quickly.

5. dispatching-parallel-agents — obra/superpowers — 7,500 installs
   Why: You coordinate Grind agents. Parallel dispatch patterns — how to structure work across multiple agents, handle failures, and synthesize outputs — are directly applicable to your coordination role.

6. subagent-driven-development — obra/superpowers — 8,700 installs
   Why: You work with and orchestrate other agents. Understanding how to structure tasks for subagents, specify outputs, and review results makes your coordination more effective.

7. turborepo — vercel — 6,000 installs
   Why: MCM spans multiple file types and build processes. Monorepo coordination patterns — even without Turborepo itself — apply to how you manage the build pipeline.

8. expo-cicd-workflows — expo — 5,300 installs (closest to CI/CD patterns on skills.sh)
   Why: CI/CD pipeline patterns for multi-platform projects. MCM is static HTML but the deployment pipeline (Marcus zips and sends to Kai) benefits from formal CI/CD thinking.

9. azure-observability — microsoft/github-copilot-for-azure — 16,200 installs
   Why: Infrastructure monitoring patterns. Your watchdog script and agent coordination system need observability — structured logging, health checks, alert thresholds.

10. writing-plans — obra/superpowers — 12,400 installs
    Why: Your .agent-protocol.md and .agent-status.md are planning artifacts. Structured planning methodology improves the documents you write to coordinate the org.

BEYOND SKILLS.SH (where skills.sh is thin for your domain):
- GitHub Actions advanced patterns (docs.github.com/actions): Even if MCM does not use GitHub Actions yet, the CI/CD pattern library is the best reference for build pipeline design. Start with reusable workflows and matrix strategies.
- Shell scripting best practices (Google Shell Style Guide): Your coordination scripts benefit from formal shell scripting standards — error handling, logging, idempotency.
- pre-commit framework (pre-commit.com): Enforce quality gates at commit time for all Grind agents. One config file, run by all contributors — this is the structural enforcement layer for repo hygiene.

START HERE: verification-before-completion (platform changes need structural gates, not intentions) and dispatching-parallel-agents (your core coordination skill). Those two directly address your highest-impact responsibilities.

FR — Research Lead, Forge
